answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds agent registration to a cryptographic beacon verifying continuous zero-knowledge proof of unique work. Registering identity clusters requires provably burning stake derived from compressed shale reserve commitments. The slashing protocol enforces superlinear cost scaling where provisioning n concurrent nodes scales verification expenses at O(n^2.5). Any malicious coordinated cluster triggers a stake-destruction ripple across linked entities, imposing exponential capital loss on the attacker.
